title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Bannerman Personnel
tiers.description: All executive and non-executive directors, full-time, part-time and casual employees, and contractors and consultants of Bannerman and Bannerman group companies. Insider trading, short-term/speculative dealing, hedging of unvested entitlements and blackout-period rules apply uniformly to this group.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors (including alternate directors); the defined term 'director' includes any related party of the director. Distinguished for clearance (Chairman, or Chairman of the Audit Committee if the dealing director is the Chairman), for the express permission to deal in third-party financial products hedging a vested holding, and for expanded post-trade disclosure (including information needed for the Company's ASX change-of-interest notices).

tiers.name: Employees, Contractors and Consultants
tiers.description: Employees, contractors and consultants who are not directors; distinguished only for clearance (Chief Executive Officer) and a shorter post-trade confirmation.

definitions.hedging_definition: any transaction which would have the effect of hedging or otherwise transferring to any other person the risk of any fluctuation in the value of any unvested entitlement in Bannerman securities

windows.end_anchor: conclusion of two business days following the release of the Quarterly Activities and Cashflow Reports relating to the previous quarter

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Board and/or Chief Executive Officer may advise other blackout periods (e.g. prior to announcement of a significant matter to ASX). Not stated whether confidential.

rules.detail: Securities covered by the policy expressly include derivatives and other financial products issued by third parties in relation to Bannerman shares, options and performance rights, with no exchange-traded limitation. Dealing in such a product therefore requires the same prior written clearance, no-inside-information confirmation and blackout compliance as dealing in shares.
rules.evidence: derivatives (such as exchange-traded options and warrants) and other financial products issued by third parties in relation to Bannerman shares, options and performance rights

rules.detail: Directors and employees who participate in a Bannerman equity-based incentive plan must not hedge or otherwise transfer to another person the risk of value fluctuation in any unvested share, performance right or option still subject to time or performance hurdles.
rules.evidence: you must not enter into any transaction which would have the effect of hedging or otherwise transferring to any other person the risk of any fluctuation in the value of any unvested entitlement in Bannerman securities.

rules.detail: Directors are expressly permitted to deal in financial products issued by third parties which operate to limit the economic risk of a vested holding, subject to prior written Chairman consent, no inside information, no blackout period and no short-term/speculative dealing.
rules.evidence: you can deal in Bannerman securities (or financial products issued by third parties in relation to Bannerman securities which operate to limit the economic risk of a vested holding in Bannerman securities) provided ... you obtain the prior written consent of the Chairman

rules.detail: Hedging of a vested holding by a non-director is not named as permitted (unlike directors under 5.2(a)); it is caught only because a hedging product is a 'financial product ... in relation to Bannerman shares' within the Securities definition, so it is subject to ordinary CEO clearance as a dealing.
rules.evidence: subject to the rules of any applicable Bannerman equity-based plan, you can deal in Bannerman securities at any time provided you obtain the prior written consent of the Chief Executive Officer

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar arrangement over Bannerman shares is an 'agreement to do' a trading transaction, or a financial product in relation to Bannerman shares, and so is a dealing requiring the same clearance as any other dealing.
rules.evidence: trading in securities (i.e. subscribing for, buying, selling or entering into an agreement to do any of those things)

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy; only 'short term or speculative dealing' is prohibited, which is a distinct concept.
Securities lending is not named and is not listed in the dealing definition.

CFDs are not named. A CFD referencing Bannerman shares is a 'financial product ... in relation to Bannerman shares' and so a dealing requiring clearance; a short CFD would also engage the short-term/speculative dealing ban.
rules.evidence: derivatives (such as exchange-traded options and warrants) and other financial products issued by third parties in relation to Bannerman shares, options and performance rights

rules.detail: A margin loan (or other financing arrangement carrying a risk that Bannerman securities will be traded under its terms) is not banned but requires prior written consent of the Chairman (Chairman of the Audit Committee if the borrower is the Chairman) and disclosure of key terms, quantity, trigger points, the lender's unilateral sale right and other material details.
rules.evidence: You are not permitted to enter into a margin loan or other financing arrangement where there is a risk that Bannerman securities will be traded pursuant to the terms of the margin loan or financing arrangement (together a Margin Loan), unless you have obtained prior written consent of the Chairman to enter into the Margin Loan and disclose to the Chairman the following information regarding the Margin Loan (Loan Information)

rules.detail: Granting security over Bannerman securities is not named separately, but it falls within the broad 'Margin Loan' definition (any financing arrangement carrying a risk securities will be traded under its terms) and so requires the same Chairman consent and Loan Information disclosure. A charge unconnected to any financing (and to any risk of forced trading) is not addressed.
rules.evidence: or other financing arrangement where there is a risk that Bannerman securities will be traded pursuant to the terms of the margin loan or financing arrangement

rules.detail: Not limited to margin loans: 'other financing arrangement' where trading risk exists is covered, so a loan secured on the collared shares is permitted with prior written Chairman consent and disclosure of Loan Information, with no outright prohibition and no distinction by vesting state.
rules.evidence: You are not permitted to enter into a margin loan or other financing arrangement where there is a risk that Bannerman securities will be traded pursuant to the terms of the margin loan or financing arrangement (together a Margin Loan), unless you have obtained prior written consent of the Chairman

rules.detail: Blanket, undefined ban on short term or speculative dealing; no period or basis is specified.
rules.evidence: You must not engage in short term or speculative dealing in Bannerman securities.

clearance.approver: Chairman (Chairman of the Audit Committee if the dealing director is the Chairman)
clearance.post_trade_to: person to whom prior notice was given, and the Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: you obtain the prior written consent of the Chairman (or the Chairman of the Audit Committee if you are the Chairman) ... this approval to trade is valid for only five (5) clear business days from the date indicated below, unless otherwise revoked earlier by notice in writing.

clearance.post_trade_to: Chief Executive Officer and Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: you obtain the prior written consent of the Chief Executive Officer ... this approval to trade is valid for only five (5) clear business days from the date indicated below, unless otherwise revoked earlier by notice in writing.

short_term.evidence: You must not engage in short term or speculative dealing in Bannerman securities.

exceptions.approver: Chairman (or Chairman of the Audit Committee or Chief Executive Officer in his absence)
Chairman (or Chairman of the Audit Committee or Chief Executive Officer in his absence)
exceptions.evidence: in order to comply with an undertaking given to, or an order by, a court
acquire ordinary shares in the Company by conversion of securities giving a right of conversion to ordinary shares
acquire Bannerman securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class
acquire Bannerman securities under a dividend reinvestment plan, a rights issue or a share purchase plan that is available to all holders of securities of the same class
acquire, or agree to acquire, options or performance rights under a Company share incentive plan
exercise options acquired under a Company share incentive plan (but may not sell all or any of the shares received upon exercise of the options other than in accordance with this policy)
transfer the Bannerman securities already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the relevant Bannerman person is a beneficiary
invest in, or trade units of, a fund or other scheme where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party
provide undertakings to accept, or accept, a takeover offer

financing_disclosure: All Bannerman Personnel; trigger: before entering into a margin loan or other financing arrangement carrying a risk that Bannerman securities will be traded under its terms; to: Chairman (Chairman of the Audit Committee if the borrower is the Chairman); deadline: prior consent required, i.e. before entering into the arrangement.

external_documents: Rules of Bannerman's applicable equity-based incentive plan(s)
exemption_authority: Chairman (or, in his absence, Chairman of the Audit Committee or Chief Executive Officer) may permit a sale-only dealing during a blackout period in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order/undertaking, or other circumstances the Chairman determines), provided no inside information exists. Board may approve other exceptions to blackout periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You are not permitted to enter into a margin loan or other financing arrangement where there is a risk that Bannerman securities will be traded pursuant to the terms of the margin loan or financing arrangement ... unless you have obtained prior written consent of the Chairman
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike an outright ban, the loan leg of a funded collar is achievable with Chairman consent and disclosure of the Loan Information, making BMN more accommodating than policies with a blanket secured-financing prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: disclose to the Chairman the following information regarding the Margin Loan (Loan Information): key terms; number of Bannerman securities involved; the trigger points; the right of the lender to sell the securities unilaterally; and any other material details.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's collar-linked loan documentation (LVR triggers, enforcement/unilateral sale rights) would need to be disclosed to the Chairman up front and kept current if terms change.

bespoke_clauses.topic: vested-holding hedge expressly permitted for directors
bespoke_clauses.clause: you can deal in Bannerman securities (or financial products issued by third parties in relation to Bannerman securities which operate to limit the economic risk of a vested holding in Bannerman securities)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put/call legs of a collar over a director's vested shares are expressly contemplated by the policy, not merely swept in by a general dealing definition, reducing interpretive risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If you are the Chairman of Bannerman and you intend to enter into a Margin Loan, you must obtain the prior written consent of the Chairman of the Audit Committee
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar counterparty relationship involves the Chairman personally, sign-off shifts to the Audit Committee Chairman rather than creating a self-approval conflict.

bespoke_clauses.clause: this approval to trade is valid for only five (5) clear business days from the date indicated below, unless otherwise revoked earlier by notice in writing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar (and its loan) must be executed within 5 business days and can be revoked before then, so timing certainty is lower than a longer or open-ended clearance window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: “director” means a director of Bannerman and includes any related party of the director.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a related party or family entity of a director does not avoid the director-level consent and disclosure requirements.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the right of the lender to sell the securities unilaterally
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy requires disclosure of the lender's unilateral sale right but does not state whether a lender-triggered forced sale during a blackout period is excused, leaving enforcement timing risk unresolved.

summary: A funded collar over vested Bannerman shares looks achievable, though not risk-free. Hedging is banned only for unvested equity-incentive entitlements (4.2); for a director, dealing in third-party financial products that limit the economic risk of a vested holding is expressly permitted with prior written Chairman consent (Audit Committee Chairman if the director is the Chairman himself), confirmation of no inside information, and avoidance of blackout periods and short-term/speculative dealing; for non-director employees the same protection is available only via the general dealing definition and CEO clearance. The loan leg is not banned: any margin loan or 'other financing arrangement' carrying a risk that shares will be traded under its terms requires prior written Chairman consent plus disclosure of key terms, quantity, trigger points and the lender's unilateral sale rights. Clearance, once given, is valid for only five business days and is revocable by notice, so the collar and loan documentation should be ready to execute quickly once approved, and must sit outside the quarterly blackout window (and any ad hoc blackout) unless the Chairman grants a sale-only exception for hardship or court order. The policy does not address whether a lender's forced sale during a blackout period is excused or requires fresh clearance, which should be clarified contractually with the bank.
